items.title: 54271_Charlie Holmes oral history interview
items.q: So Mr. Mills said, 'Well, we'll replace Holmes

ctx.x: So they cut the trip short, and Mills brought the band into New York. And we all got together, and he wanted to know what was the trouble. So it looked like nobody wanted to speak up about the money, so I opened my mouth -- and I was about one of the least interested parties in getting anything; I had never spoken up for no money or anything. I spoke up, I opened my mouth, thinking somebody else would back me up. And I told him, I said, 'Well, the men don't think we're getting paid enough.'

So Mr. Mills looked at me. 'Anybody else got anything to say?' Nobody said a word. So Mr. Mills said, 'Well, we'll replace Holmes, and the rest of the schedule will go down.' And there I am sittin' like a fool. And that was it. What was there to do after that? I come out the band; that was it. That's the reason I got out of it.
Well, you made a few recordings with the band.
